_note: THE ESCALATED PATH (parity F12). Everything past `pick` reaches the store, and this corpus pins the three things that are subtle: (1) an ungranted bulk read REFUSES and names the fix rather than prompting on the caller's behalf, (2) iOS 17+ limited contact access is a GRANT over a shared subset, reported as access:"limited" with only that subset returned, and (3) paging arithmetic, which is the same on all three renderers even though the underlying cursor is not (an enumeration offset on iOS, a SQL LIMIT/OFFSET on Android). Runners: TS (@despia-native/kernel contacts-core.ts, contacts-conformance.test.ts), Kotlin (:core ContactsCore, ContactsConformanceTest), Swift (Engine/iOS/ContactsCore.swift, ContactsConformance in the record lane).

paging._note: { total, limit, offset } -> what one `list` page reports. `endCursor` is present only when there IS a next page, so a caller that loops until endCursor is absent terminates.

cases.name: the first of several pages
a middle page
the LAST page carries no cursor
an exact multiple still terminates rather than offering an empty page
an empty book is one empty page
a limit past the cap clamps to 500 rather than fetching the world
a zero or negative limit clamps to 1, never to unbounded

access._note: authorization -> what `list` does. `limited` is a GRANT over a shared subset, not a soft denial. The refusal MESSAGE must name `permission`, because a caller that cannot find the fix retries the same call forever.

cases.name: full access enumerates and reports granted
iOS 17 limited access returns ONLY the shared subset and says limited
undetermined refuses and does NOT prompt
denied refuses the same way
a device policy denial is `restricted`, which is not recoverable by asking again

write._note: A limited read grant carries NO write right, and the write refusal names the write level specifically.

cases.name: a full grant writes
limited access is a read subset, not a write grant
an empty contact is refused before any store call
a contact with only an email is meaningful enough to save

shape._note: The vCard round-trip: what goes in comes back, with labels normalised to the shared vocabulary (home | work | mobile | main | other) rather than the platform's own constant.

cases.name: labels normalise across platforms
an unknown platform label folds to other
a birthday is an ISO date, never a locale string
a nameless contact still has a display name
